title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' sequel to La Longue Marche (c. 1981-82). Grothendieck is building algebraic, linear 'shadows' of his profinite Teichmüller-type groups (Ĝ_{0,3}, T̂_{0,3}, M_{0,3}).

Setting. S is a base scheme and G is a group scheme over S, a form of GL(2) or of a quotient of GL(2). ρ and σ are two sections of G satisfying the 'general conditions' of earlier pages, plus the extra condition Tr σ = 0. He notes the constructions could be done without that condition (using 𝒢_{ρ,σ} instead of 𝒢*_{ρ,σ}), but keeps it for convenience. One may normalize ρ, σ so that Tr(ρ+σ) = 1.

The group scheme 𝒢_{ρ,σ}. It was defined on the preceding pages, formulas (29). Its points are data (α, β, μ, ε, λ) together with an element u of G such that:
- u ρ u^{-1} = ξρ, with ξ = α ρ(λ)^{-1}, i.e. u ρ u^{-1} = int(α)(ρ^λ);
- u σ u^{-1} = ε int(β)(σ), with ε = ±1;
- det u = μ.
This is a linearized version of the 'équation des lacets'. An automorphism sends each generator to a conjugate of a λ-th power, up to the sign ε.

This page. He defines the scheme
 SM_{ρ,σ} = S𝒢*_{ρ,σ} ×_S SG,
with sections (α, β, μ, ε, f), where f is an arbitrary section of SG (≅ SL(2)_S). At this point it is only a product of schemes. The group law, a twisted (semidirect-type) one, is to be defined on the next page. There he constructs a profinite group M̃_{0,3} with a canonical multiplicative map into this product. M̃_{0,3} is an extension by Ẑ^3 whose elements are tuples (u, g_0, g_1, g_∞) with u(ℓ_i) = int(g_{u(i)}^{-1})(ℓ_{u(i)}^λ): automorphisms together with chosen conjugating elements.

The basic example. S = Spec Ẑ, ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (trace 1, det 1, ρ^3 = -1), σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]] (trace 0, σ^2 = -1). One checks ρσ = [[1,0],[1,1]], a unipotent (parabolic) element. So (σ, ρ, ρσ) are the standard order-2, order-3 and parabolic generators of PSL2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3. They are the images of the three 'lacets' of the orbifold M_{1,1}, i.e. P^1 with cone points of orders 2, 3, ∞.

This yields a canonical homomorphism
 Ĝ_{0,3} → G(Ẑ)^{±1} ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)^{±1}/(±1),
landing in the classes of det ±1. On the next page the orientation-preserving part Ĝ^+_{0,3} goes to SL(2,Ẑ)/(±1). In effect each lacet-preserving automorphism, read on the congruence quotient PSL2(Ẑ), is realized by conjugation by a det ±1 matrix, with det -1 for orientation reversal.

The margin note says that later he prefers variants of these groups ('SoM_{ρ,σ}', p. 559 ff).

Purpose: replace the profinite Teichmüller/GT-type groups by group schemes defined by explicit equations over an arbitrary base. These track the action of Ĝ_{0,3} on the image of the fundamental group in GL2/PGL2 together with an SL2 part.
errors: Possible notational inconsistency, probably in the transcription or a slip: with G = GL(2)_S one does not have G(Ẑ) ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)/(±1). The isomorphism in (2), and the next page's SL2(Ẑ)' = SL(2,Ẑ)/(±1), suggest G is GL(2)/μ_2 or a PGL-type quotient. Then 'SG ≅ SL(2)_S' should read SL(2)/μ_2. Alternatively the subscript in 'G_1 = GL(2)_S' indicates a different group.

The group structure on SM_{ρ,σ} is not yet defined on this page; only the underlying scheme is. The multiplication rule on the next page is itself hedged ('ou un truc analogue (à gauche / à gauche!)').

The checks are fine: ρ has trace 1 and order 6 in SL2 (order 3 projectively); σ has trace 0 and order 4 (order 2 projectively); Tr(ρ+σ) = 1 matches the stated normalization; ρσ is unipotent, as the lacet relation requires.

ideas.what: Group scheme 𝒢_{ρ,σ} of solutions of a linearized 'équation des lacets' in a GL2-type group scheme over an arbitrary base: u ρ u^{-1} = int(α)ρ^λ, u σ u^{-1} = ε int(β)σ, det u = μ.
ideas.modern_name: algebraic/linear shadow of GT-type equations; comparable to the image of GT or G_Q acting on the congruence completion of SL2(Z), and to relative/weighted completions of π_1(M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT action on Γ̂_{1,1}: Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps (1990s); relative completion of SL2(Z) with Galois action: Hain–Matsumoto (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished notes, as far as I know. Esquisse mentions the Teichmüller tower and GT-type group but not this scheme.

ideas.what: SM_{ρ,σ} = S𝒢*_{ρ,σ} ×_S SG, to receive a twisted group structure making the canonical map from M̃_{0,3} multiplicative.
ideas.modern_name: semidirect-type extension of a GT-shadow by SL2; analogue of the arithmetic or Teichmüller group of M_{1,1} mapping to its congruence image

ideas.what: Canonical homomorphism Ĝ_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)^{±1}/(±1), sending the orientation-preserving part to PSL2(Ẑ). It uses the identification of the lacets of the (2,3,∞) orbifold with σ, ρ, ρσ in PSL2(Z).
ideas.modern_name: action of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group on (P)SL2(Z)^ followed by projection to the congruence quotient; the det giving a sign or cyclotomic-type character
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and Γ_{1,1} but not this explicit map

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up group schemes over an arbitrary base S, cut out by explicit 'lacet' equations on generators of order 2 and 3 in a GL2-type group. These are meant as schematic receptacles for GT/Teichmüller-type profinite groups via a canonical multiplicative map. This scheme-theoretic linear model of the lacet equations, valid over any base and with the sign ε, does not seem to be studied in the literature. The literature instead works with profinite or pro-unipotent/relative completions over Q.
missed.quote: On désigne par SM_{ρ,σ} le schéma produit (1) SM_{ρ,σ} = S𝒢*_{ρ,σ} ×_S SG
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give an integral/arithmetic algebraic model of the image of GT in congruence quotients of SL2. This complements the Hain–Matsumoto relative completion and work on GT acting on Γ̂_{1,1}.

missed.claim: The lacet equation for P^1 - {0,1,∞} is transported to the (2,3,∞) orbifold / PSL2(Z) picture via the explicit matrices ρ, σ with ρσ parabolic. The homomorphism to GL2(Ẑ)^{±1}/±1 is read with det -1 encoding orientation reversal. This is an explicit link between Ĝ_{0,3} and congruence data of the modular group.
missed.quote: on a donc un homomorphisme canonique (2) Ĝ_{0,3} → G(Ẑ)^{±1} ≃ GL(2,Ẑ)^{±1}/(±1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Related results (GT acting on Γ̂_{1,1}, Galois images on SL2) exist but are usually credited to 1990s authors. This is a documented early instance in Grothendieck's own notes.

deep.surprise_reason: A coherent, unpublished scheme-theoretic construction linking the lacet equation to explicit SL2 data, with a planned group structure. The underlying phenomenon (GT acting on congruence quotients of the modular group) is known in spirit, and the page is mostly set-up, so the surprise is modest.
transcription_corrections: 'faire leurs constructions ainsi dans cette condition' likely reads 'faire nos constructions sans cette condition supplémentaire'.
'mais par impondérables dans tout pour la suite' is uncertain; probably something like 'mais par commodité nous la supposons dans toute la suite'.
'on trouve un donc un homomorphisme canonique' likely reads 'et ainsi on a donc un homomorphisme canonique'.
'(cf p. ex. par ρ, σ 477')' is probably a page reference such as 'cf p. ex. p. 477''.
'G = GL(2)_S' may be 'G_1 = GL(2)_S' or a quotient of GL(2); this is consistent with G(Ẑ) ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)/(±1).
Margin: 'Pour la suite, la préférence des variantes' likely reads 'Pour la suite, il est préférable [d'utiliser] des variantes des groupes SM_{ρ,σ}, cf SoM_{ρ,σ}, cf p. 559 ff'.
'A = Ẑ)' has a stray closing parenthesis.
